newsitem.title: FINLAND: Raisio says J&J to develop Benecol.
newsitem.headline: Raisio says J&J to develop Benecol.

text.p: Finnish food group Raision Tehtaat said on Tuesday its new U.S. partner on the key ingredient of its Benecol margarine had a great desire to contribute to developing the product.

Raisio earlier annouced giving an exclusive marketing right to Johnson & Johnson company McNeil to use Raisio's Benecol stanol ester in a variety of forms to be introduced in the North American market, including Mexico, Canada and Puerto Rico.
"They have a big desire to contribute to developing the brand," Raisio Executive Vice President Tor Bergman told a news conference.

"They have very big resources and channels to the retail market in the United States, or in other words everything that Raisio did not have," Bergman said, adding that there would now be efforts to make Benecol "a global mega-brand".
"Margarine will be just one in a broad series of Benecol products," Bergman said.
Raisio CEO Matti Salminen said global marketing would become easier if Benecol becomes a brand name in the U.S. He expected it to take two to three years for the business to get off the ground there.

Asked whether Johnson & Johnson could become a partner also in Europe, Bergman said at this stage the partners had only focused on North America. "Europe and Japan are the next areas, and the work has begun," he said but did not elaborate.
"(The deal) will free up resources in other areas because Johnson & Johnson will handle the Benecol business in the United States," Salminen told Reuters after the news conference.
"It will have a significant impact on earnings in the long term, but will also have an effect this year," he said, but he declined to give any detail on the earnings impact.
